A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strong emission-line radio galaxies are more likely to be star-forming, while weak-line objects are not.
strong emission lines in AGNs are associated with more vigorous star formation in the host galaxy, and this star formation is probably triggered by the AGN itself.

the radio luminosity of the AGN is a poor indicator of the star formation rate in the host galaxy, and that the optical emission line class is a better predictor.
